entries.t: Heat resistance of PLA, PETG, ABS and ASA
entries.g: heat resistant petg, abs heat, how hot can petg get, glass transition, softening temperature, car dashboard print
entries.a: Printed plastics soften near their glass transition: PLA about 55–60 °C, PETG about 75–80 °C, ABS and ASA about 100–105 °C, nylon and polycarbonate higher still. Keep the working temperature 10–20 °C below that under load. A car in summer sun reaches 70–80 °C inside, so use ABS, ASA or PC there, not PLA or PETG.

entries.g: how deep footings, footing depth, frost line, frost depth, post footing depth, foundation depth
entries.a: Footings must sit on undisturbed soil and below the local frost line, with at least 12 in below grade under the US residential code. Frost depth runs from almost 0 in the far south to 4–5 ft or more in the northern US, so check the local building department. Deck post footings are commonly 8–12 in diameter or 16–24 in square pads, sized for the load and the soil bearing capacity.

entries.t: Concrete bags for a fence or deck post
entries.g: bags of concrete post, concrete volume for a post hole, how much concrete for a post, quikrete post hole, 80 lb bag yield
entries.a: Bag yields: an 80 lb bag makes about 0.60 ft³, a 60 lb bag about 0.45 ft³, a 50 lb bag about 0.375 ft³. A 10 in hole 3 ft deep holds about 1.64 ft³; less a 4x4 post (0.26 ft³) that leaves about 1.4 ft³, so buy 3 × 80 lb bags (2.3 needed). Hole diameter should be about 3× the post width, and depth about ⅓ to ½ of the post height above ground, below frost.
